jobs.excerpt: About RivetRivet is an AI-native accounting company.
jobs.description:
About Rivet

Rivet is an AI-native accounting company. In less than 3 years, we've built a T500 accounting company in the US, combining corporate and personal income tax, sales tax, R&D credits, and bookkeeping into a single, all-inclusive experience that eliminates the worst parts of tax season for real businesses and the people who run them.

Our platform is designed to feel invisible: it guides clients through their tax to-dos, automates the drudgery for preparers, and gets out of the way when it's not needed. We measure success in time saved and returns completed, not vanity usage metrics. We run Rivet (the business) on Rivet (the platform) because owning the stack makes it possible to deeply embed AI into every step of our workflows, far more than our competition will ever be able to relying on third-party/off-the-shelf tooling.

Our team of 75 supports more than 1,300 clients, including some of the most innovative companies in the US — Cursor, Cognition, and ModRetro — and their executives, investors, and employees.

And while we may have just gotten started a little over two years ago, this isn't our first rodeo:

  • Nick Abouzeid (cofounder & CEO) comes from Ramp, where he ran three of their Growth teams from $100M → $600M in ARR

  • Kyle Christenson (cofounder & Head of Tax) comes from the IRS, where he spent six years as an auditor before leaving to start his own firm over a decade ago

We're well-funded, growing quickly, and sustainable. We've raised over $7M to date, from investors like XYZ Ventures, Susa Ventures, Haystack Ventures, and 40+ executives from Ramp, Anduril, Physical Intelligence, & more.

Why this role is different

The product is the only part of tax season most of our clients ever see, and it runs through one design engineer today. Every module's back-end owner pairs with him on the UI, which makes him the shared dependency for every screen we ship. You'd be the second, and the two of you would split it.

  • Ownership from first commit to production. Engineers design, build, ship, and maintain their work — no handoffs, no middle-management mazes.

  • Decisions happen at the edge. Engineers talk to clients and tax preparers directly. We optimize for speed and context, not committee consensus.

  • Clear is kind. We surface problems early, talk about tradeoffs openly, and don't sugarcoat. We're kind by being honest, not by being vague.

  • Pragmatic stacks. We pick tools that solve real problems. If it doesn't help us ship faster, safer, or better, we don't use it.

  • Skin in the game. We ship things we'd be proud to put our name on — and if something breaks, we own it and fix it fast.

Our stack

Six engineers today, four languages. You'd live mostly in the first two:

  • Frontend: React and TanStack, deployed to Cloudflare Workers. Typed clients generated from protobuf.

  • Platform: Go, as a modular monolith — Connect RPC over protobuf, Go Fx for wiring, sqlc and goose against Postgres, River Pro for background jobs, Watermill for pub-sub over RabbitMQ.

  • AI and eval: Python, in their own repos — ModelBridge (a gRPC service for AI building blocks) and TaxBench, our internal eval suite.

  • Legacy integration: a C# Windows agent that drives Drake, one of the tax platforms our industry never built APIs for.

  • Infrastructure: AWS — ECS Fargate, Amazon MQ, AMP, Loki, Tempo — provisioned by Pulumi, itself written in Go.

  • Around the edges: Buildkite for CI, OpenTelemetry throughout, Doppler for secrets, Linear for tracking.

What you'll do

  • Drive on our client-facing surface area end to end — the portal where clients hand over documents, answer questions, and watch a return move toward filed. Design, build, ship, and keep it working.

  • Build the workspace our preparers live in all day. Roughly 75 accountants use our internal tooling for eight hours a day, four months a year. Speed and clarity are the whole product for them.

  • Work closely with Anton, our design engineer, and the rest of our engineering team. Back-end isn't off-limits - you'll have the ability to build and influence how our entire product is built from end-to-end.

  • Ship AI into the interface, not around it. Extraction, review, and suggestion flows only work if the UI makes it obvious what the model did and where a human needs to look.

  • Talk to the people using it. Accountants are in our Slack; clients are one call away. Watch someone use what you built before you decide it's done.

We're fully distributed — but if you want an office, we'll help you find one through our investor network.

What makes you a fit

  • 6+ years building production web applications, primarily in React

  • Have owned a product surface end to end, including the parts after launch

  • Can read and write enough backend code to unblock yourself rather than filing a ticket and waiting

  • Care about the unglamorous parts — loading states, error handling, what happens on a bad connection with a 40MB PDF

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-changing, early-stage environment

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Nice to haves

  • Production experience with TanStack (Query, Router, Table)

  • Deployed to the edge — Cloudflare Workers or similar

  • Worked with generated clients from protobuf, gRPC, or Connect RPC

  • Built document-heavy or upload-heavy interfaces, where files are large, messy, and occasionally encrypted

  • Strong design sense, especially if you've shipped without a dedicated designer

  • Built internal tools for operators who sit close enough to tell you what's broken

  • Built tax-adjacent software — fund administration, payroll, accounting platforms, filing systems, anywhere a wrong number has consequences

What we offer

  • Benefits and meaningful equity

  • A fully remote team, plus twice-yearly company offsites

  • A well-funded, fast-moving environment with minimal layers of management

  • A world-class client base that values your time and pays for the premium experience

  • The chance to build production-grade software your teammates use and love every day

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every qualification. Strong candidates rarely check every box.

Buscamos un especialista con experiencia sólida para operar, automatizar y asegurar la plataforma cloud que soporta las aplicaciones de uno de los proyectos más importantes de la empresa, desplegada principalmente en AWS y con cargas en Oracle Cloud (OCI). El objetivo de este rol es llevar la plataforma a un nivel de estabilidad, seguridad y cumplimiento homogéneo con los estándares de la compañía y mantenerlo a lo largo de la siguiente etapa de crecimiento. Trabajarás de manera estrecha con las 5 personas del equipo de infraestructura y con el equipo de desarrollo.

Tareas y responsabilidades principales:

  • Operar y mantener la plataforma cloud (AWS y OCI).
  • Administrar cargas serverless y clústeres de Kubernetes gestionados.
  • Gestionar API gateways (Kong) y la integración de las aplicaciones con el proveedor de identidad corporativo (Okta).
  • Mantener la infraestructura como código con Terraform y los pipelines de despliegue con GitLab CI y ArgoCD (GitOps).
  • Operar las bases de datos PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis y la mensajería (RabbitMQ): mantenimiento, copias de seguridad y pruebas de restauración.
  • Gestionar la observabilidad (Prometheus, Grafana) y el alertado; responder a incidentes y realizar análisis de causa raíz.
  • Gestionar identidades y accesos (IAM) en ambas nubes y aplicar las políticas de seguridad y cumplimiento de la compañía.
  • Documentar la plataforma: runbooks, diagramas y procedimientos operativos.
  • Colaborar con los equipos de desarrollo y coordinarse con proveedores externos.

Requisitos imprescindibles:

  • Experiencia práctica con AWS en producción: VPC y redes, EC2, EKS, IAM, S3, Route53, balanceadores.
  • Administración de Kubernetes: upgrades, grupos de nodos, RBAC, ingress controllers y troubleshooting de pods y red.
  • Terraform: módulos, estado remoto, gestión de varios entornos.
  • CI/CD: pipelines de infraestructura y aplicaciones con GitLab CI o similar.
  • Linux y redes: administración de sistemas, routing, VPN, TLS y certificados, DNS, firewalls.
  • Scripting: Bash y Python (o lenguaje equivalente) para automatización.
  • Observabilidad: Prometheus y Grafana o herramientas equivalentes.
  • Más de 3 años operando infraestructura cloud en producción (incidentes, actualizaciones, migraciones), con responsabilidad directa sobre al menos un entorno productivo.

Certificación deseable:

  • AWS SysOps Administrator, CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator), AWS Solutions Architect Associate.

Lo que ofrecemos:

•Salario competitivo según experiencia.

  • Plan de carrera técnico (no es obligado crecer a roles de gestión).
  • Trabajo con un dominio técnico no trivial: criptografía, regulación europea, infraestructura QTSP.
  • Equipo pequeño con autonomía real, sin capas innecesarias.

• Modalidad de trabajo: remoto 100 %.

  • Incorporación estructurada y paquete de beneficios atractivo.

jobs.excerpt: The Product Owner, Universal Gateway, owns the backlog for the single ingress and egress layer that carries DICOM studies and HL7 messages into and out of Intelerad's cloud platform, serving IntelePACS, InteleArchive, InteleShare VNA, InteleViewer, and InteleOrchestrator.
jobs.description:
The Product Owner, Universal Gateway, owns the backlog for the single ingress and egress layer that carries DICOM studies and HL7 messages into and out of Intelerad's cloud platform, serving IntelePACS, InteleArchive, InteleShare VNA, InteleViewer, and InteleOrchestrator. Universal Gateway replaces today's product-specific gateways, relays, and edge servers with one standardized service for DIMSE and DICOMweb traffic, HL7 routing and normalization, authentication, and multi-tenant isolation. This is a hands-on, technically deep role: the Product Owner works day-to-day with platform engineering, SRE, and Hosting teams, and ensures that what gets built is reliable enough for clinical imaging workflows where downtime directly affects patient care.

Acting as the primary connection point between the Product Manager's vision and the development team's execution, the Product Owner combines deep knowledge of DICOM, HL7, and healthcare integration with hands-on agile delivery experience on platform or infrastructure products. Success in this role depends on sound day-to-day judgment: making trade-off decisions that keep delivery aligned to the broader product strategy set by Product Management and business leaders. This is not a generalist Product Owner role. Candidates should bring direct, hands-on experience with medical imaging interoperability, integration engines, or healthcare connectivity infrastructure. In your application, please describe a specific DICOM, HL7, or healthcare integration problem you owned and how you resolved it.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own and prioritize the product backlog for Universal Gateway, writing clear user stories and acceptance criteria for DICOM DIMSE (C-STORE, C-FIND, C-MOVE, Storage Commitment, MWL), DICOMweb (STOW-RS, QIDO-RS, WADO-RS), HL7 v2 inbound and outbound messaging, and pathology whole slide imaging (WSI) ingestion.
  • Partner daily with engineering and design throughout the development lifecycle — refinement, sprint planning, stand-ups, reviews, and retrospectives — making timely trade-off decisions on scope, sequencing, and priority, and escalating strategic or financial trade-offs to the Product Manager or Director as needed.
  • Define and validate non-functional requirements, including failover SLA, RTO/RPO, multi-AZ high availability, and throughput and latency targets by modality (CR through large CT, mammography, and WSI), and confirm delivered features meet them along with DICOM PS3.4 conformance and the published DICOM Conformance Statement.
  • Gather and synthesize input from Sales, Customer Success, Support, and customers to inform backlog refinement, and support the Product Manager with market research, competitive analysis, and feature-level requirements.
  • Track and report on sprint and release progress, velocity, and delivery metrics, proactively flagging risks to scope or timeline, and incorporate feedback from user acceptance testing and beta programs into subsequent backlog iterations.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, business, technology, or equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years of experience as a Product Owner, Technical Product Manager, or integration or interface engineer, including at least 2 years on platform, infrastructure, or integration products rather than end-user feature applications.
  • Working knowledge of agile/scrum methodologies and hands-on experience with backlog and sprint management tools such as Jira or Azure DevOps.
  • Hands-on working knowledge of DICOM (DIMSE services, DICOMweb, AE title configuration, conformance statements) and HL7 v2 (ADT, ORM, ORU), demonstrated by writing requirements for, configuring, or troubleshooting DICOM or HL7 interfaces in production.
  • Experience partnering directly with engineering teams, with comfort leading technical discussions on feasibility, sequencing, and trade-offs, including high availability, failover, and multi-region design for Linux-based, containerized services.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail in requirements definition and quality validation.
  • Working understanding of cloud infrastructure and operations, including AWS or equivalent, containers, infrastructure as-code (such as Terraform and Ansible), networking (load balancers, VPN, TLS and mTLS), and observability tooling.

Preferred Qualifications & Special Requirements

  • Experience with medical imaging systems (PACS, VNA, RIS) or integration engines and routers (such as Mirth/NextGen Connect, Rhapsody, Cloverleaf, or DICOM routing products).
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through influence rather than authority.
  • Exceptional communication and organizational skills, with a track record of collaboration across engineering, design, and cross-functional business teams.
  • Experience defining SLAs, RTO/RPO, or reliability targets for clinical or other mission-critical systems.
  • Familiarity with multi-tenant SaaS architectures, tenant isolation, and healthcare security and privacy obligations (HIPAA, GDPR, or equivalent).
  • Exposure to digital pathology (whole slide imaging) or high-volume modality workflows such as mammography and large CT. This job description is not a comprehensive list of tasks or requirements and Intelerad reserves the right to change it at any time.

    o Evaluate and implement security solutions that enhance the organization's security posture.

Experience working with cloud service providers such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud to deploy and optimize cloud-based applications. Familiarity with best practices in cloud automation, cost management, and operational monitoring.

jobs.title: Flutter & Node.js Fullstack Engineer (f/m/d) - Fully Remote
jobs.excerpt: memodio is a digital health application (DiGA) fighting forgetfulness and dementia 🧠 Our app is prescribed by doctors, fully reimbursed by German statutory health insurance, and recommended by leading medical associations.
jobs.description:
memodio is a digital health application (DiGA) fighting forgetfulness and dementia 🧠 Our app is prescribed by doctors, fully reimbursed by German statutory health insurance, and recommended by leading medical associations. In a clinical trial with 140 participants, we showed that it measurably improves memory performance, everyday independence, and quality of life. More than 10,000 people already trust memodio.

We've been on the market for over five years. So we have the speed and ownership culture of a startup, without the chaotic early days: a validated product, paying reimbursement partners, and real users who notice when we ship something good. Now we're growing the engineering team.

Where you sit: anywhere in the world. We're a small distributed team, not a company with a remote policy bolted on. The one requirement is overlap: at least four hours of your working day between 09:00 and 18:00 Berlin time, because we solve problems together, not by throwing tickets over a wall.

How you join us: as an employee or as a freelancer, whichever fits your situation better. Tell us which you'd prefer when you apply.

Tasks

Our core product is live and helping thousands of people, but it's far from finished. A big part of this role is evolving the existing app to better fit the people who actually use it: adults aged 50+, often dealing with early-stage cognitive decline. Every improvement you make has a direct, visible effect on someone's day.

Beyond the core product we're building new and adjacent products, including ones with AI capabilities. If working with LLMs excites you, there's real room to shape that. If it doesn't, that's fine too.

How the role works

You won't get finished designs and implementation specs to execute. You'll get problems, context, and user needs and the freedom to figure out the best solution. That's deliberate: it's where the creativity and the ownership live. It also means the job asks you to think about what to build, not only how.

Today our CTO is hands-on in the codebase, supported by a part-time engineer. You'd join as the next full-time engineer on a small team where your decisions carry real weight.

Day to day

  • Frontend: evolve our Flutter app (iOS & Android), with a strong focus on good UX and usability for people aged 50+
  • Backend: design and build our Node.js APIs and services for new features
  • Product: work closely with our medical and product colleagues: your voice matters in what we build and how
  • Quality: help us keep code review, testing, and engineering standards at the level a regulated medical product demands
  • Optional: if DevOps interests you, there's room to shape our cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, and deployment but it isn't the core of the job

Requirements

What you bring

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, and we care far more about what you've actually shipped than about the number. Show us something you built
  • Flutter/Dart skills, or a proven ability to ramp up fast (e.g. coming from React Native or native mobile)
  • Working knowledge of Node.js and building APIs, you don't have to be equally strong on both ends, but you can't be mobile-only
  • You work well remotely and asynchronously. This is a distributed role on a tiny team. You write clearly, you post updates without being asked, you unblock yourself, and you don't go quiet for two days
  • At least four hours of daily overlap with 09:00–17:00 Berlin time (CET/CEST)
  • You're comfortable working from underspecified problems. As a small company we can't hand you full designs and implementation plans — you'll need to ask the right questions, propose solutions, and make calls. In return, you get creative freedom
  • A self-directed, structured way of working, you thrive with a lot of ownership and little supervision
  • Dedication: we don't do inhumane startup hours, but when it matters - a release, a deadline, a critical fix
  • Fluent English, written and spoken. German is a plus, not a requirement

Nice to have, not required

  • Interest or experience in software security, our product passed an intense security audit and we intend to keep that bar high
  • Experience with accessibility, or with building for older users
  • Experience with DiGA, medical devices, or other regulated environments
  • Startup or consultancy background
  • DevOps experience (CI/CD, cloud infrastructure)

You are probably not right if

  • You need a large team around you. For now it's you, a hands-on CTO, and a part-time engineer. Specialists to hand things off to come later, you'll help hire them
  • You're looking for greenfield-only work. A big part of this job is improving a live product with real users and real constraints
  • You need someone to hand you tickets, or a manager checking in daily. Remote and self-directed is the whole shape of this role
  • You see your scope as highly specialised. We need technical solutions for internal tooling here and there too. If touching a HubSpot integration feels beneath you, this isn't the right place

Benefits

What we offer

  • Purpose: your code measurably helps people — clinically proven, prescribed by doctors, reimbursed by statutory health insurance
  • Real ownership: as the next full-time engineer, you'll own features end to end and have a direct say in how we build
  • Stability with startup energy: 5+ years on the market, revenue from reimbursement partners
  • Genuinely remote, genuinely worldwide: work from wherever you're based, with flexible hours around a light overlap window. Our office in Potsdam is there if you ever want it
  • Your choice of setup: employment or freelance, whichever suits you
  • No office politics: a small, focused team where the energy goes into the product, not into positioning
  • Straight talk: you've just read our salary range and a list of reasons not to apply. That's how we operate internally too

If you have any questions, please don't hestitate to reach out :)
The initial phase will be a short questionnaire, followed by a small project and 1-2 live interview rounds.

jobs.excerpt: About Sayari: Sayari is the judgment infrastructure for trustworthy AI in economic security and commercial risk.
jobs.description:
About Sayari:

Sayari is the judgment infrastructure for trustworthy AI in economic security and commercial risk. The Sayari Commercial World Model resolves 11.7B+ primary-source records from 250+ jurisdictions forming the ground truth of global commerce. A Judgment Ontology, encoding over a decade of investigative tradecraft, and Superconductor, an agentic orchestration platform, deliver AI that reasons like an expert analyst, shows its work, and traces every finding to its source. Trusted by U.S. Customs and Border Protection, HM Revenue & Customs, and Fortune 500 enterprises, Sayari is used by thousands of professionals across 35+ countries to secure supply chains and dismantle illicit networks. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., with offices in London, Singapore, Tokyo, and Tel Aviv.

About the Role

Sayari’s customers buy answers to hard problems: who really owns a supplier, where a sanctioned network is moving goods, which alerts deserve an analyst’s time. Sayari’s AI platform Superconductor delivers those answers at machine scale. It is built in the field, with analysts and engineers working alongside customers to define what it needs to do.

The Field Intelligence Analyst brings Sayari’s tradecraft to that work. You scope the problem, design the solution, prove its value, and deliver mission impact. You own the analytical relationship for a portfolio of accounts, from first conversation through sustained delivery. What you learn on live engagements flows back into Superconductor and into Sayari’s tradecraft standard.

You work in our Field Intelligence Department, a global team of analysts deployed to support government agencies and Fortune 500 companies. You sit in the same org as Forward Deployed Engineers and the Product team. The field shapes the roadmap, and Product sets it.

Why This Role Exists

  • Customers buy answers. Superconductor reasons like an expert analyst at machine scale. The analyst’s job shifts from producing every answer by hand to directing, validating, and extending what Superconductor produces, and teaching customer analysts to do the same.
  • Context should survive the contract. The analyst who designed the proof-of-value knows why the success criteria are what they are. Keeping that analyst on the account protects delivery quality and surfaces the next problem before the customer names it.
  • Tradecraft is built in the field. Field Intelligence Analysts see what was promised, what was delivered, and what the customer did with it. That full view produces better methodology, better evals, and a better Superconductor than any single-phase role can.

What You Will Do

Own the analytical relationship, end to end

  • Run discovery and proof-of-value engagements anchored on work the customer already pays people to do, such as alert adjudication, due diligence, investigations, and case prioritization. Define success criteria you will personally be accountable for delivering.
  • Stay on the account after close and deliver the work you scoped. This includes multi-hop investigations across ownership, trade, and corporate records, plus analytical briefings and training.
  • Serve as the customer’s single analytical point of contact from first conversation through renewal.

Build with Field Engineering and Product

  • Pair with FDEs on discovery and delivery. You define the analytical requirement, they build it, and you validate it against the mission.
  • When something built for one customer should be rebuilt for many, make the case to Product with evidence: the problem, the workaround, and the customers who share it.
  • Document where the platform falls short of the mission, with raw examples attached.

Deliver analyst-plus-AI, and teach it

  • Direct Superconductor against live mission problems. Validate its reasoning against expert standards, and extend it into new customer workflows.
  • Train and certify customer analysts on Sayari methods and on working with Superconductor. Identify the customer experts who should go further.

Build the tradecraft

  • Capture the judgment calls, non-obvious pivots, and creative approaches from live engagements. Contribute them to the Tradecraft team as expert-annotated reference cases, eval scenarios, and training material.
  • Hold your work to the Field Intelligence standard, and help raise it.

Support Go-To-Market Teams

  • Work with Sales to diagnose customer problems, scope solutions, and deliver mission impact.

Who You Are

Required

  • A builder’s temperament and comfort with ambiguity. You do well on small teams with end-to-end ownership and no defined lane, working next to engineers on things that don’t exist yet.
  • Experience conducting complex, multi-source investigations in one or more of these areas: financial crime, sanctions and export controls, supply chain and forced labor risk, transnational criminal organizations, or law enforcement and intelligence investigations. This should include work with corporate records, trade data, and OSINT.
  • Customer-facing range. You have scoped engagements, demonstrated capability to skeptical experts, and delivered under a statement of work. Candidates often come from solutions consulting, services delivery, embedded analytics, or mission-support roles.
  • Hands-on fluency directing and evaluating AI and agentic analytical tools. You can define what “right” looks like precisely enough to test against.
  • Clear communication with analysts, program managers, engineers, and executives.

Desired

  • Python or SQL for data manipulation, and familiarity with REST APIs.
  • Experience designing training curricula or certifying analysts.
  • For government portfolios: an active Government security clearance and same citizenship as your country of residence.

The target base salary for this position is $X-$Y plus COMPANY BONUS/COMMISSION and equity. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including location, local market variances, candidate experience and expertise, internal peer equity, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Benefits:

  • 100% fully paid medical, vision, and dental for employees and their dependents
  • Generous time off; we observe all US federal holidays, close our office for a winter break (12/24-12/31), in addition to granting 18 PTO days and 10 sick days
  • Outstanding compensation package; competitive commissions for revenue roles and bonuses for non-revenue positions
  • A strong commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion

  • A collaborative and positive culture - your team will be as smart and driven as you
